notes: Plain lettering the menus draw from common_2d_tex/1 (the 16x16 number font with its comma, colon, point and signs, the 8x16 save-slot font whose "comma" is the date's slash, and the DAY-, MONEY, NY, TIME and PRICE labels), drawn in the game's outline font (ui/text.json) while post_process.sharp_text is on, fitted to each sprite's rectangle as the battle panels' text_replacements are. Turning sharp text off draws the atlas again. Stylised lettering (the result and schedule fonts, the PAUSE pill, GO!, NOW LOADING) stays an image; the YES/NO/OK pills are sprite_shapes.json outlines under futura text.

Entries take the battle panels' text_replacements fields: source (image and rect, matched exactly), text, and optionally region, colour, stroke_width, centered and line_pitch. shadow is drawn under all of them and the battle panels' lettering: offset in 640x480 units, colour and alpha (0 for none). The bitmaps carry a dark shadow of their own one pixel down and right; the default matches it.

Display lettering: an entry with font names one of fonts, an installed outline face (the first of faces found, after loading files privately), drawn as a whole string whose ink fills region at the window's own resolution. erase redraws the art with region (or erase_region, which may reach over a painted shadow) filled row by row from the texels at its two ends (leaning by erase_slant, else slant), or with the flat erase_fill; without erase the art outside region is drawn and the lettering inside it not; art false draws nothing of a lettering-only sprite. outline (colour, outline_width in canvas units) and shadow (offset, colour, alpha, blur) edge the text. Several entries on one sprite are all drawn over one erased art. colour is the art's ink colour, tinted as the sprite is. When no face of the font is installed the art is drawn as it was.

classes: an entry's "class" names one of classes, whose keys it takes unless it sets them itself; a class may name another class, so a family shares one font, colour, slant, shadow or erase setting and changing the class restyles every entry of it. opacity (0 to 1, default 1) is the ink's own alpha, for translucent lettering such as REGULATION. within and measure are for tools/sprite_lettering.py only: "measure" fills region and erase_region for entries without one from the art, finding the ink near colour inside within (tolerance, summed over the channels), leaving out straight rules min_line long or more, splitting labels where gap texels of space part them, growing the erase box by grow [l, t, r, b], and with clear_edges leaving out ink touching within's edges (a frame or pill border in the ink's colour); several entries on one sprite with one colour and within take its labels in reading order. "add batch.json" merges a batch's classes and replacements, "preview out.png --match text" draws each matched sprite beside its replacement, and "adopt" moves entries' repeated keys onto their class.
